# Issue #15208 weighted-aggregation candidate

`avg_<base>` and `average_<base>` totals use `count_<base>` weights when every contributing average has a count and the total weight is positive; otherwise behavior falls back to the prior arithmetic mean. Regressions cover unequal group sizes, both average prefixes, and the no-count fallback. Targeted Vitest remains to run in a bootstrapped checkout because this mount has no Node/pnpm toolchain.

# Pivot average aggregation contract

Memory type: semantic_memory
Recorded: 2026-08-16T02:27:08.097515+00:00
Confidence: 1.00
Owner: Sana Farid
Tags: langfuse, analytics, weighted-average, contract, issue-15208

## Summary

Subtotal and grand-total averages over pre-aggregated groups must use Σ(mean_i × count_i) / Σcount_i when a matching count_<base> metric exists. Both avg_<base> and average_<base> naming are supported. If complete usable counts are unavailable or total weight is non-positive, preserve the arithmetic-mean fallback.

item.aggregated_output: # Agent Guidelines for Langfuse Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform for developing, monitoring, evaluating, and debugging AI applications. ## How To Work - Read the minimal local context required for the task. - Keep changes scoped and avoid unrelated refactors. - If you are about to write a `useEffect` — or sync fetched data into state, or wire form initial values from loaded data — read `.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md` first. Most such effects should not exist. - For bug fixes, write the failing test first, confirm it fails, then fix the bug. If the bug depends on a data shape, pause and ask: can `pnpm run seed` prefill that shape locally? If not, consider extending a seeder scenario so the bug stays cheaply reproducible (`packages/shared/scripts/seeder/AGENTS.md`), or note why a seed cannot express it. - For user-visible frontend changes in `web/**`, review the affected flow in a real browser before signoff. Prefill the data the flow needs with the seed CLI (`pnpm run seed -- list` shows scenarios; runs print UI deep links) — never with ad-hoc scripts or raw ClickHouse inserts. - When fixing an isolated styling issue in an individual component, read `.agents/skills/storybook/SKILL.md` create or update a component story following its guidance first. - Every PR auto-builds (via GitHub Actions) a disposable, full-stack preview at `pr-.preview.langfuse.com` — nothing to spin up. Use the `langfuse-previews` skill to use or debug one, e.g. read a preview's web/worker error logs with `kubectl`. - For documentation screenshots in Markdown, avoid fixed `height` on `` tags; prefer Markdown images or width-only HTML so previews preserve aspect ratio. - When working on the search bar or any filtering UI/grammar, read `web/src/features/search-bar/README.md` first. It owns the grammar ↔ `FilterState` contract, the validate/lower parity invariants, and the cross-view extension playbook — the bar is intended to become the primary filter interface for every filterable view, so new filtering work extends it through that contract rather than forking it. - When adding or modifying any chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Do not add or widen ESLint disable comments or config overrides without explicit user approval for the exact rule and scope. - Always quote file paths in shell commands, or use `noglob` for path-heavy commands, to avoid zsh glob expansion issues with dynamic Next.js routes. - Never invoke Node-installed binaries through `./node_modules/.bin/*`. Always run them through `pnpm`. - Never commit secrets or credentials. Keep `.env*.example` files in sync with required env vars. ## Project Structure ```text langfuse/ |- web/ # Next.js app (UI + tRPC + public REST) |- worker/ # Queue consumers and background processing |- packages/shared/ # Shared domain, DB, queue contracts, repositories |- ee/ # Enterprise package consumed by web |- generated/ # Generated API clients (do not hand-edit) |- fern/ # API definition sources `- scripts/ # Repo scripts ``` - Dependency direction: - `web` -> `@langfuse/shared`, `@langfuse/ee` - `worker` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/ee` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/shared` -> no imports from `web`, `worker`, or `ee` - Queue payload schemas and queue-name contracts are owned by `packages/shared/src/server/queues.ts`. - High-signal shared entry points: - Domain models: `packages/shared/src/domain/{observations,traces,scores}.ts` - Postgres schema: `packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma` - ClickHouse migrations: `packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/{clustered,unclustered}/*.sql` - Architecture principles live in `.agents/ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md`. ## Core Commands - Install deps: `pnpm install` - Dev all packages: `pnpm run dev` - Dev web only: `pnpm run dev:web` - Dev worker only: `pnpm run dev:worker` - Lint all: `pnpm run lint` - Typecheck all: `pnpm run typecheck` / `pnpm tc` - Run a single test file (vitest filters on the filename argument): - web server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` (client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client `) - worker: `pnpm --filter worker run test ` - shared: `pnpm --filter @langfuse/shared run test ` - Build check: `pnpm run build:check` - Full build: `pnpm run build` - Worktree bootstrap: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` - Worktree maintenance: `bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` - Install Playwright Chromium: `pnpm run playwright:install` ## Local Data Inspection - For feature testing and debugging, inspect the local databases directly when it helps you understand the existing test data. Prefer read-only queries, and continue to use the seed CLI to create frontend test state rather than ad-hoc inserts. - Dev Docker Compose exposes these clients on `${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}`: - Postgres: `PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres}" psql -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}" -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres}"` - ClickHouse: `clickhouse client --host "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" --port "${CLICKHOUSE_NATIVE_PORT:-9000}" --user "${CLICKHOUSE_USER:-clickhouse}" --password "${CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD:-clickhouse}" --database default` - Redis: `REDISCLI_AUTH="${REDIS_AUTH:-myredissecret}" redis-cli -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${REDIS_HOST_PORT:-6379}"` - If any connection fails, check `docker-compose.dev.yml` for local override variables and confirm the services are running. ## Verification - `web/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted web tests. - `worker/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted worker tests. - `packages/shared/**` non-schema changes: `pnpm run lint` plus one targeted web check and one targeted worker check. - `packages/shared/prisma/**` or `packages/shared/clickhouse/**`: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run db:generate`, and targeted web/worker regressions. - Public API contracts in `web/src/pages/api/public/**`, `web/src/features/public-api/types/**`, or `fern/apis/**`: `pnpm run lint`, targeted server API tests, and Fern update/regeneration. - Cross-package refactors: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and targeted tests for impacted packages. - Client-bundle soundness: CI scans every prod web build (`pnpm run scan:client-bundle`) for minifier-dropped bindings and Node-only globals leaking into browser chunks — the SWC dropped-binding class ships runtime-only `ReferenceError`s that dev builds and type checks cannot see (LFE-10645). On failure, `scripts/scan-client-bundle.mjs`'s header explains the canonical fix. End your turn with evidence, not claims: quote each check's summary line — e.g. `Tasks: 8 successful, 8 total` (turbo lint/typecheck) or `Tests 12 passed (12)` (vitest) — say which checks you skipped and why, never report unverified work as done, and never end with work pending. ## Generated Files Do not hand-edit generated or build artifacts: - `generated/*` - `web/.next/*` - `web/.next-check/*` - `*/dist/*` - `packages/shared/prisma/generated/*` Public API contract changes must update Fern sources in `fern/apis/**` and regenerated outputs. Never hand-edit `generated/**`. ## Shared Agent Setup - `.agents/AGENTS.md` is the canonical root guide. - Root `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`. - Root `CLAUDE.md` is a compatibility symlink to `AGENTS.md`. - When creating or editing `.agents/skills/**`, use `.agents/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`; keep skills concise with progressive disclosure. - After changing shared agent setup, run `pnpm run agents:sync` and `pnpm run agents:check`. - Generated provider config and shim outputs under `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.codex/`, `.vscode/`, or `.mcp.json` are local artifacts, not source of truth files. fatal: not a git repository (or any parent up to mount point /mnt/chronos-enterprise-state-division-v2/infra-v1-realistic-v2-20260815/host/states/01-chronos/state/checkouts) Stopping at filesystem boundary (GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM not set).

/**

 * Uses a recursive algorithm to handle N dimensions dynamically instead of hardcoded cases
 *
 * Features:
 * - Supports any number of dimensions up to MAX_PIVOT_TABLE_DIMENSIONS

 * Algorithm:
 * 1. Recursively groups data by each dimension in order
 * 2. At each level, processes remaining dimensions for nested structure

## Summary

Subtotal and grand-total averages over pre-aggregated groups must use Σ(mean_i × count_i) / Σcount_i when a matching count_<base> metric exists. /**
 * Transforms flat query results into nested pivot table structure with totals and subtotals
 * Uses a recursive algorithm to handle N dimensions dynamically instead of hardcoded cases
 *
 * Features:
 * - Supports any number of dimensions up to MAX_PIVOT_TABLE_DIMENSIONS
 * - Creates subtotals at each dimension level except the deepest
 * - Proper indentation and nesting for hierarchical data
 * - Grand total calculation across all data
 * - Row limiting applied before processing for performance
 *
 * Algorithm:
 * 1. Recursively groups data by each dimension in order
 * 2. At each level, processes remaining dimensions for nested structure
 * 3. Adds subtotals for non-leaf dimension groups
 * 4. Creates data rows at the deepest level with full dimension path
 * 5. Appends grand total row at the end
 *
 * @param data - Array of raw database rows from query
 * @param config - Configuration for pivot table generation
 * @returns Array of processed rows ready for table rendering

  "body": "## Summary\n\nWhile differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs \u2014 they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:\n\n1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.\n2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.\n\nBoth live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I've verified the neighbouring inter-rater stats (`calculateCohensKappa`, `calculateWeightedF1Score`, `calculateOverallAgreement`) against scikit-learn and they are **correct** (0 mismatches over 1,200 random cases) \u2014 these two are the outliers.\n\n---\n\n## Bug 1 \u2014 Numeric score histogram bins on rounded values\n\n**File:** `web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts` \u2192 `createHistogramData` (rendered by the dashboard `NumericScoreHistogram`, produced in `dashboard-router.ts`).\n\nThe value is rounded to 2 decimals before its bin index is computed, while the bin edges are not:\n\n```ts\nconst min = round(Math.min(...numericScoreValues));            // rounded\nconst binSize = range / bins || 1;\n// ...\nconst shiftedValue = round(value) - min;                       // value rounded to 2dp\nconst binIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(shiftedValue / binSize), bins - 1);\n```\n\n### Reproduction (vs `numpy.histogram`)\n\nA faithful port of the function was run against `numpy.histogram` (same bin count) over 1,200 random score datasets:\n\n```\nuniform 0..1 (n=50)          | value-in-wrong-bucket:185/200  numpy-mismatch:117/200\nuniform 0..1 (n=200)         | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:199/200\nnarrow 0.80..0.85 (n=40)     | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:200/200\n1..5 likert (n=60)           | value-in-wrong-bucket:  0/200  numpy-mismatch:  0/200\n...\nruns differing from numpy.histogram: 916 / 1200\n```\n\nInteger (Likert) scores are unaffected \u2014 which is why this has gone unnoticed \u2014 but any fractional scores (0\u20131 confidence, LLM-judge scores, cost, latency) are misbinned.\n\n**Minimal deterministic case** (7 equal-width bins over `[0, 1]`, input `[0, 0.857, 0.86, 1]`):\n\n| value  | bucket it's counted in (current) | bucket that contains it |\n| ------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- |\n| 0.857  | **`[0.86, 1]`** \u274c               | `[0.71, 0.86]`          |\n\n`round(0.857) = 0.86`, so `floor(0.86 / (1/7)) = 6` \u2192 the **top** bucket, even though `0.857 < 0.86`.\n\nA second symptom of the same rounding: for narrow ranges the 2-decimal **labels collapse**, e.g. `createHistogramData([0.855, 0.857, 0.858, 0.861])` produces buckets labeled `[\"[0.85, 0.85]\", \"[0.85, 0.86]\"]` \u2014 a zero-width bucket and duplicated edges.\n\n### Fix\n\nBin on the raw value (`Math.floor((value - min) / binSize)`), derive edges from the raw min/max, and round only the **display labels** (with enough precision to keep edges distinct). After the fix the port matches `numpy.histogram` exactly (**0 / 1200** mismatches).\n\n---\n\n## Bug 2 \u2014 Pivot-table subtotals average the averages\n\n**File:** `web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts` \u2192 `applyAggregation` / `calculateSubtotals` (subtotal & grand-total rows in dashboard pivot-table widgets).\n\n```ts\ncase \"avg\":\n  return values.reduce((sum, val) => sum + val, 0) / values.length;   // mean of per-row means\n```\n\nEach pivot data row is already an aggregate (e.g. `avg_cost` over `count` items). Averaging those per-row averages **unweighted** only equals the true overall average when every group has the same size.\n\n### Reproduction\n\nThe repo's own test data (and its docstring example) demonstrates it. `calculateGrandTotals` over:\n\n```\n{ count: 10, avg_cost: 0.5 }\n{ count: 15, avg_cost: 0.6 }\n{ count: 20, avg_cost: 0.2 }\n{ count: 25, avg_cost: 0.4 }\n{ count:  5, avg_cost: 0.8 }\n```\n\n| quantity                              | value      |\n| ------------------------------------- | ---------- |\n| **shown** (avg of averages) `\u03a3avg/5`  | **0.5**    |\n| **correct** (weighted) `\u03a3(avg\u00b7count)/\u03a3count = 32/75` | **0.4267** |\n\nThe dashboard silently overstates average cost by ~**17%** here. The existing test even encodes the wrong value:\n\n```ts\navg_cost: 0.5, // (0.5 + 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.8) / 5\n```\n\n(`percentile` subtotals have the same problem and are already flagged as \"a reasonable approximation\" in the code.)\n\n### Fix\n\nWeight each row's value by its `count` when a count metric is present:\n`\u03a3(avg_i \u00b7 count_i) / \u03a3(count_i)`. This makes subtotal/total averages exact for the common case (a count column is present) and falls back to the previous unweighted behavior when no weights are available. The truly exact fix for percentiles is query-level (the database can recompute over raw rows), but count-weighting is a strict improvement.\n\n---\n\n## Methodology\n\nEach function was ported 1:1 to JS and executed against reference implementations:\n`numpy.histogram` (Bug 1), and `sklearn.metrics.{cohen_kappa_score, f1_score, accuracy_score}` for the neighbouring categorical stats (verified correct \u2014 not bugs). Repro scripts and a proposed patch with unit tests are available; happy to open a PR.",

{
  "artifact_type": "issue",
  "author": "hassaanch23",
  "body": "## Summary

While differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs — they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:

1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.
2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.

Both live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I've verified the neighbouring inter-rater stats (`calculateCohensKappa`, `calculateWeightedF1Score`, `calculateOverallAgreement`) against scikit-learn and they are **correct** (0 mismatches over 1,200 random cases) — these two are the outliers.

---

## Bug 1 — Numeric score histogram bins on rounded values

**File:** `web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts` → `createHistogramData` (rendered by the dashboard `NumericScoreHistogram`, produced in `dashboard-router.ts`).

The value is rounded to 2 decimals before its bin index is computed, while the bin edges are not:

```ts
const min = round(Math.min(...numericScoreValues));            // rounded
const binSize = range / bins || 1;
// ...
const shiftedValue = round(value) - min;                       // value rounded to 2dp
const binIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(shiftedValue / binSize), bins - 1);
```

### Reproduction (vs `numpy.histogram`)

A faithful port of the function was run against `numpy.histogram` (same bin count) over 1,200 random score datasets:

```
uniform 0..1 (n=50)          | value-in-wrong-bucket:185/200  numpy-mismatch:117/200
uniform 0..1 (n=200)         | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:199/200
narrow 0.80..0.85 (n=40)     | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:200/200
1..5 likert (n=60)           | value-in-wrong-bucket:  0/200  numpy-mismatch:  0/200
...
runs differing from numpy.histogram: 916 / 1200
```

Integer (Likert) scores are unaffected — which is why this has gone unnoticed — but any fractional scores (0–1 confidence, LLM-judge scores, cost, latency) are misbinned.

**Minimal deterministic case** (7 equal-width bins over `[0, 1]`, input `[0, 0.857, 0.86, 1]`):

| value  | bucket it's counted in (current) | bucket that contains it |
| ------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 0.857  | **`[0.86, 1]`** ❌               | `[0.71, 0.86]`          |

`round(0.857) = 0.86`, so `floor(0.86 / (1/7)) = 6` → the **top** bucket, even though `0.857 < 0.86`.

A second symptom of the same rounding: for narrow ranges the 2-decimal **labels collapse**, e.g. `createHistogramData([0.855, 0.857, 0.858, 0.861])` produces buckets labeled `["[0.85, 0.85]", "[0.85, 0.86]"]` — a zero-width bucket and duplicated edges.

### Fix

Bin on the raw value (`Math.floor((value - min) / binSize)`), derive edges from the raw min/max, and round only the **display labels** (with enough precision to keep edges distinct). After the fix the port matches `numpy.histogram` exactly (**0 / 1200** mismatches).

---

## Bug 2 — Pivot-table subtotals average the averages

**File:** `web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts` → `applyAggregation` / `calculateSubtotals` (subtotal & grand-total rows in dashboard pivot-table widgets).

```ts
case "avg":
  return values.reduce((sum, val) => sum + val, 0) / values.length;   // mean of per-row means
```

Each pivot data row is already an aggregate (e.g. `avg_cost` over `count` items). Averaging those per-row averages **unweighted** only equals the true overall average when every group has the same size.

### Reproduction

The repo's own test data (and its docstring example) demonstrates it. `calculateGrandTotals` over:

```
{ count: 10, avg_cost: 0.5 }
{ count: 15, avg_cost: 0.6 }
{ count: 20, avg_cost: 0.2 }
{ count: 25, avg_cost: 0.4 }
{ count:  5, avg_cost: 0.8 }
```

| quantity                              | value      |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| **shown** (avg of averages) `Σavg/5`  | **0.5**    |
| **correct** (weighted) `Σ(avg·count)/Σcount = 32/75` | **0.4267** |

The dashboard silently overstates average cost by ~**17%** here. The existing test even encodes the wrong value:

```ts
avg_cost: 0.5, // (0.5 + 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.8) / 5
```

(`percentile` subtotals have the same problem and are already flagged as "a reasonable approximation" in the code.)

### Fix

Weight each row's value by its `count` when a count metric is present:
`Σ(avg_i · count_i) / Σ(count_i)`. This makes subtotal/total averages exact for the common case (a count column is present) and falls back to the previous unweighted behavior when no weights are available. The truly exact fix for percentiles is query-level (the database can recompute over raw rows), but count-weighting is a strict improvement.

---

## Methodology

Each function was ported 1:1 to JS and executed against reference implementations:
`numpy.histogram` (Bug 1), and `sklearn.metrics.{cohen_kappa_score, f1_score, accuracy_score}` for the neighbouring categorical stats (verified correct — not bugs). Repro scripts and a proposed patch with unit tests are available; happy to open a PR.",

Great bug report — I've verified both issues in the codebase and can confirm they're real.

**Bug 1 — Histogram rounding before binning**: The `createHistogramData` function in [`score-analytics-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts#L73-L78) does indeed call `round(value)` (which truncates to 2 decimal places via `toFixed(2)`) before computing `shiftedValue / binSize`. **Bug 2 — Unweighted average of averages**: The `applyAggregation` function in [`pivot-table-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts#L497-L498) computes `values.reduce(...) / values.length` for the `"avg"` case — a simple arithmetic mean of the per-group averages with no count-weighting. There's also a [related prior issue (#13331)](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/13331#issuecomment-4307081217) about histogram bucket overflow in the score comparison view, which stems from similar histogram-edge computation problems.

Hi @hassaanch23! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I'm helping the Langfuse team.

Great bug report — I've verified both issues in the codebase and can confirm they're real.

**Bug 1 — Histogram rounding before binning**: The `createHistogramData` function in [`score-analytics-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts#L73-L78) does indeed call `round(value)` (which truncates to 2 decimal places via `toFixed(2)`) before computing `shiftedValue / binSize`. The bin edges are derived from rounded min/max as well, so fractional scores near bin boundaries get placed in the wrong bucket exactly as you describe.

**Bug 2 — Unweighted average of averages**: The `applyAggregation` function in [`pivot-table-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts#L497-L498) computes `values.reduce(...) / values.length` for the `"avg"` case — a simple arithmetic mean of the per-group averages with no count-weighting. The `calculateSubtotals` function calls this without passing group counts [[1]](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts#L525-L546), so there's no way it can produce a correct weighted result for groups of unequal size.

There's also a [related prior issue (#13331)](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/13331#issuecomment-4307081217) about histogram bucket overflow in the score comparison view, which stems from similar histogram-edge computation problems.

Your proposed fixes (bin on raw values + round only labels; weight averages by count when available) both sound correct. A PR with the repro tests you mentioned would be very welcome.

**Histogram fix** (`createHistogramData`): bin on the raw value (no rounding before `floor`), derive edges from the raw min/max, and round only the display labels with 3-decimal precision so narrow-range edges stay visually distinct.

**Pivot-table fix** (`calculateSubtotals`/`calculateGrandTotals`): when a `count_<base>` column is present (the same SQL emits both columns), weight each row's `avg_<base>` by its count — `Σ(avg_i × count_i) / Σ(count_i)`. Falls back to the unweighted mean when no count column is available, so no caller breaks.

This record belongs to langfuse-analytics-evaluation-correctness: Qualify Langfuse analytics and evaluation semantics, especially aggregation, histogram, and historical trace correctness. The working evidence is langfuse/langfuse#15208 https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/15208. Samantha Roy qualifies the pinned upstream behavior, uses a temporary downstream patch only when an operational boundary requires it, and records contribution, removal, and rollback criteria before rollout. Company context: # Company Overview: Redwood Inference\\n\\n## Company name + 1\\u2011liner\\n**Redwood Inference** is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\n## Mission and thesis\\n**Mission:** Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.\\n\\n**Thesis:** As LLM capabilities and open model ecosystems expand, competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to *serving*: latency, cost, reliability, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling. The winners will provide a unified runtime and developer experience that makes inference predictable and economical across rapidly changing  Initiative context: # Developer Experience (SDKs, Quickstarts, Usage Analytics) Connector guidance: Directory:\\nsources/confluence\\n\\nTarget number of files:\\n5000\\n\\nFile name format:\\nFile names should be short and descriptive with words connected with dashes (e.g. company-pto-policy-2025.json).\\n\\nContent rules:\\n- All of the documents must be associated with a space (directory), they cannot be at the top level directly under confluence.\\n- Confluence is Redwood Inference\\u2019s formal internal documentation system.\\n- Documents should read like polished, broadly consumable references (not personal scratchpads). Write in complete sentences with clear structure.\\n- Use standard Confluence-style organization Pinned source: langfuse/langfuse@c4eaf1f4c0cd1851f0c9dbea2802c243cf787a09. Public record excerpt: issue #15208. ## Summary\\n\\nWhile differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs \\u2014 they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:\\n\\n1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.\\n2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.\\n\\nBoth live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I\\n\\nProcedure\\n\\n1. Reproduce the behavior against the pinned source tree.\\n2. Record operational impact and compatibility constraints.\\n3.   "artifact_type": "confluence",
  "author": "Samantha Roy",
  "content": "Summary\n\nRedwood Inference maintains langfuse/langfuse as an upstream-first infrastructure dependency.   "artifact_type": "issue",
  "author": "hassaanch23",
  "body": "## Summary\n\nWhile differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs \u2014 they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:\n\n1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.\n2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.\n\nBoth live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I've verified the neighbouring inter-rater stats (`calculateCohensKappa`, `calculateWeightedF1Score`, `calculateOverallAgreement`) against scikit-learn and they are **correct** (0 mismatches over 1,200 random cases) \u2014 these two are the outliers.\n\n---\n\n## Bug 1 \u2014 Numeric score histogram bins on rounded values\n\n**File:** `web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts` \u2192 `createHistogramData` (rendered by the dashboard `NumericScoreHistogram`, produced in `dashboard-router.ts`).\n\nThe value is rounded to 2 decimals before its bin index is computed, while the bin edges are not:\n\n```ts\nconst min = round(Math.min(...numericScoreValues));            // rounded\nconst binSize = range / bins || 1;\n// ...\nconst shiftedValue = round(value) - min;                       // value rounded to 2dp\nconst binIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(shiftedValue / binSize), bins - 1);\n```\n\n### Reproduction (vs `numpy.histogram`)\n\nA faithful port of the function was run against `numpy.histogram` (same bin count) over 1,200 random score datasets:\n\n```\nuniform 0..1 (n=50)          | value-in-wrong-bucket:185/200  numpy-mismatch:117/200\nuniform 0..1 (n=200)         | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:199/200\nnarrow 0.80..0.85 (n=40)     | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:200/200\n1..5 likert (n=60)           | value-in-wrong-bucket:  0/200  numpy-mismatch:  0/200\n...\nruns differing from numpy.histogram: 916 / 1200\n```\n\nInteger (Likert) scores are unaffected \u2014 which is why this has gone unnoticed \u2014 but any fractional scores (0\u20131 confidence, LLM-judge scores, cost, latency) are misbinned.\n\n**Minimal deterministic case** (7 equal-width bins over `[0, 1]`, input `[0, 0.857, 0.86, 1]`):\n\n| value  | bucket it's counted in (current) | bucket that contains it |\n| ------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- |\n| 0.857  | **`[0.86, 1]`** \u274c               | `[0.71, 0.86]`          |\n\n`round(0.857) = 0.86`, so `floor(0.86 / (1/7)) = 6` \u2192 the **top** bucket, even though `0.857 < 0.86`.\n\nA second symptom of the same rounding: for narrow ranges the 2-decimal **labels collapse**, e.g. `createHistogramData([0.855, 0.857, 0.858, 0.861])` produces buckets labeled `[\"[0.85, 0.85]\", \"[0.85, 0.86]\"]` \u2014 a zero-width bucket and duplicated edges.\n\n### Fix\n\nBin on the raw value (`Math.floor((value - min) / binSize)`), derive edges from the raw min/max, and round only the **display labels** (with enough precision to keep edges distinct). After the fix the port matches `numpy.histogram` exactly (**0 / 1200** mismatches).\n\n---\n\n## Bug 2 \u2014 Pivot-table subtotals average the averages\n\n**File:** `web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts` \u2192 `applyAggregation` / `calculateSubtotals` (subtotal & grand-total rows in dashboard pivot-table widgets).\n\n```ts\ncase \"avg\":\n  return values.reduce((sum, val) => sum + val, 0) / values.length;   // mean of per-row means\n```\n\nEach pivot data row is already an aggregate (e.g. `avg_cost` over `count` items). Averaging those per-row averages **unweighted** only equals the true overall average when every group has the same size.\n\n### Reproduction\n\nThe repo's own test data (and its docstring example) demonstrates it. `calculateGrandTotals` over:\n\n```\n{ count: 10, avg_cost: 0.5 }\n{ count: 15, avg_cost: 0.6 }\n{ count: 20, avg_cost: 0.2 }\n{ count: 25, avg_cost: 0.4 }\n{ count:  5, avg_cost: 0.8 }\n```\n\n| quantity                              | value      |\n| ------------------------------------- | ---------- |\n| **shown** (avg of averages) `\u03a3avg/5`  | **0.5**    |\n| **correct** (weighted) `\u03a3(avg\u00b7count)/\u03a3count = 32/75` | **0.4267** |\n\nThe dashboard silently overstates average cost by ~**17%** here. The existing test even encodes the wrong value:\n\n```ts\navg_cost: 0.5, // (0.5 + 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.8) / 5\n```\n\n(`percentile` subtotals have the same problem and are already flagged as \"a reasonable approximation\" in the code.)\n\n### Fix\n\nWeight each row's value by its `count` when a count metric is present:\n`\u03a3(avg_i \u00b7 count_i) / \u03a3(count_i)`. This makes subtotal/total averages exact for the common case (a count column is present) and falls back to the previous unweighted behavior when no weights are available. The truly exact fix for percentiles is query-level (the database can recompute over raw rows), but count-weighting is a strict improvement.\n\n---\n\n## Methodology\n\nEach function was ported 1:1 to JS and executed against reference implementations:\n`numpy.histogram` (Bug 1), and `sklearn.metrics.{cohen_kappa_score, f1_score, accuracy_score}` for the neighbouring categorical stats (verified correct \u2014 not bugs). Repro scripts and a proposed patch with unit tests are available; happy to open a PR.",

The bin edges are derived from rounded min/max as well, so fractional scores near bin boundaries get placed in the wrong bucket exactly as you describe.\n\n**Bug 2 \u2014 Unweighted average of averages**: The `applyAggregation` function in [`pivot-table-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts#L497-L498) computes `values.reduce(...) / values.length` for the `\"avg\"` case \u2014 a simple arithmetic mean of the per-group averages with no count-weighting. The `calculateSubtotals` function calls this without passing group counts [[1]](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts#L525-L546), so there's no way it can produce a correct weighted result for groups of unequal size.\n\nThere's also a [related prior issue (#13331)](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/13331#issuecomment-4307081217) about histogram bucket overflow in the score comparison view, which stems from similar histogram-edge computation problems.\n\nYour proposed fixes (bin on raw values + round only labels; weight averages by count when available) both sound correct. {
  "artifact_type": "issue",
  "author": "hassaanch23",
  "body": "## Summary

While differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs — they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:

1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.
2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.

Both live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I've verified the neighbouring inter-rater stats (`calculateCohensKappa`, `calculateWeightedF1Score`, `calculateOverallAgreement`) against scikit-learn and they are **correct** (0 mismatches over 1,200 random cases) — these two are the outliers.

---

## Bug 1 — Numeric score histogram bins on rounded values

**File:** `web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts` → `createHistogramData` (rendered by the dashboard `NumericScoreHistogram`, produced in `dashboard-router.ts`).

The value is rounded to 2 decimals before its bin index is computed, while the bin edges are not:

```ts
const min = round(Math.min(...numericScoreValues));            // rounded
const binSize = range / bins || 1;
// ...
const shiftedValue = round(value) - min;                       // value rounded to 2dp
const binIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(shiftedValue / binSize), bins - 1);
```

### Reproduction (vs `numpy.histogram`)

A faithful port of the function was run against `numpy.histogram` (same bin count) over 1,200 random score datasets:

```
uniform 0..1 (n=50)          | value-in-wrong-bucket:185/200  numpy-mismatch:117/200
uniform 0..1 (n=200)         | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:199/200
narrow 0.80..0.85 (n=40)     | value-in-wrong-bucket:200/200  numpy-mismatch:200/200
1..5 likert (n=60)           | value-in-wrong-bucket:  0/200  numpy-mismatch:  0/200
...
runs differing from numpy.histogram: 916 / 1200
```

Integer (Likert) scores are unaffected — which is why this has gone unnoticed — but any fractional scores (0–1 confidence, LLM-judge scores, cost, latency) are misbinned.

**Minimal deterministic case** (7 equal-width bins over `[0, 1]`, input `[0, 0.857, 0.86, 1]`):

| value  | bucket it's counted in (current) | bucket that contains it |
| ------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 0.857  | **`[0.86, 1]`** ❌               | `[0.71, 0.86]`          |

`round(0.857) = 0.86`, so `floor(0.86 / (1/7)) = 6` → the **top** bucket, even though `0.857 < 0.86`.

A second symptom of the same rounding: for narrow ranges the 2-decimal **labels collapse**, e.g. `createHistogramData([0.855, 0.857, 0.858, 0.861])` produces buckets labeled `["[0.85, 0.85]", "[0.85, 0.86]"]` — a zero-width bucket and duplicated edges.

### Fix

Bin on the raw value (`Math.floor((value - min) / binSize)`), derive edges from the raw min/max, and round only the **display labels** (with enough precision to keep edges distinct). After the fix the port matches `numpy.histogram` exactly (**0 / 1200** mismatches).

---

## Bug 2 — Pivot-table subtotals average the averages

**File:** `web/src/features/widgets/utils/pivot-table-utils.ts` → `applyAggregation` / `calculateSubtotals` (subtotal & grand-total rows in dashboard pivot-table widgets).

```ts
case "avg":
  return values.reduce((sum, val) => sum + val, 0) / values.length;   // mean of per-row means
```

Each pivot data row is already an aggregate (e.g. `avg_cost` over `count` items). Averaging those per-row averages **unweighted** only equals the true overall average when every group has the same size.

### Reproduction

The repo's own test data (and its docstring example) demonstrates it. `calculateGrandTotals` over:

```
{ count: 10, avg_cost: 0.5 }
{ count: 15, avg_cost: 0.6 }
{ count: 20, avg_cost: 0.2 }
{ count: 25, avg_cost: 0.4 }
{ count:  5, avg_cost: 0.8 }
```

| quantity                              | value      |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| **shown** (avg of averages) `Σavg/5`  | **0.5**    |
| **correct** (weighted) `Σ(avg·count)/Σcount = 32/75` | **0.4267** |

The dashboard silently overstates average cost by ~**17%** here. The existing test even encodes the wrong value:

```ts
avg_cost: 0.5, // (0.5 + 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.4 + 0.8) / 5
```

(`percentile` subtotals have the same problem and are already flagged as "a reasonable approximation" in the code.)

### Fix

Weight each row's value by its `count` when a count metric is present:
`Σ(avg_i · count_i) / Σ(count_i)`. This makes subtotal/total averages exact for the common case (a count column is present) and falls back to the previous unweighted behavior when no weights are available. The truly exact fix for percentiles is query-level (the database can recompute over raw rows), but count-weighting is a strict improvement.

---

## Methodology

Each function was ported 1:1 to JS and executed against reference implementations:
`numpy.histogram` (Bug 1), and `sklearn.metrics.{cohen_kappa_score, f1_score, accuracy_score}` for the neighbouring categorical stats (verified correct — not bugs). Repro scripts and a proposed patch with unit tests are available; happy to open a PR.",

**Bug 1 — Histogram rounding before binning**: The `createHistogramData` function in [`score-analytics-utils.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/471e150a87540ff8050b96f1233717f4c1767559/web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts#L73-L78) does indeed call `round(value)` (which truncates to 2 decimal places via `toFixed(2)`) before computing `shiftedValue / binSize`. ## Summary

Subtotal and grand-total averages over pre-aggregated groups must use Σ(mean_i × count_i) / Σcount_i when a matching count_<base> metric exists. Both avg_<base> and average_<base> naming are supported. If complete usable counts are unavailable or total weight is non-positive, preserve the arithmetic-mean fallback.
